tools.name: search_cerebrium
tools.description: Search across the Cerebrium knowledge base to find relevant information, code examples, API references, and guides. Use this tool when you need to answer questions about Cerebrium, find specific documentation, understand how features work, or locate implementation details. The search returns context

tools.name: query_docs_filesystem_cerebrium
tools.description: Run a read-only shell-like query against a virtualized, in-memory filesystem rooted at `/` that contains ONLY the Cerebrium documentation pages and OpenAPI specs. This is NOT a shell on any real machine — nothing runs on the user's computer, the server host, or any network. The filesystem is a sandb

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.description: Report a problem with this documentation site so the docs team can fix it. Use when a documentation page is incorrect, outdated, confusing, incomplete, or has a broken example. This is for feedback about the documentation content itself — not for product support requests or feedback about this tool

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "query_docs_filesystem_cerebrium" references sensitive artifacts (apikey). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "query_docs_filesystem_cerebrium" is 3229 chars, far longer than this server's median (607). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "query_docs_filesystem_cerebrium" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "query_docs_filesystem_cerebrium" appears informational but accepts parameters (command) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: query_docs_filesystem_cerebrium · Private data: query_docs_filesystem_cerebrium · Public sink: submit_feedback · Destructive: query_docs_filesystem_cerebrium.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: query_docs_filesystem_cerebrium · Private data: query_docs_filesystem_cerebrium · Public sink: submit_feedback · Destructive: query_docs_filesystem_cerebrium

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
